Subject: POC kickoff + hands-on workshop — windows and ask

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. We're excited to get the POC kickoff and the hands-on prompt review workshop on the calendar. Broad asks from our side:

- Hands-on prompt inventory review (we'll bring ~60 sample prompts across support and search).
- Routing/structured output requirements (we need a short session to align on JSON schemas and failure modes).
- A light load test to validate throughput and cold-starts for our top 10 flows.

Proposed windows (our team):
- Tue Apr 20, 10:00–13:00 PDT / 17:00–20:00 UTC
- Thu Apr 22, 09:00–12:00 PDT / 16:00–19:00 UTC

Can you:
1) Confirm which window works for the Redwood ops team,
2) Share a checklist of what you need from us beforehand (sample prompts, expected concurrency, any data classification notes).

I've attached a CSV with our initial prompt inventory (acme_prompt_inventory.csv) — it's rough but should give you an idea.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of AI Integrations | Acme Inc
priya.shah@acmeinc.com

Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on workshop — windows and ask

Thanks Priya — this is helpful. Appreciate the prompt inventory upload.

Quick answers and asks from our side:

- Both proposed windows are workable. Can you confirm whether the majority of attendees are west-coast (PDT) or EMEA? We will prioritize the window that covers the most stakeholders.

- Our recommended agenda (attached as PDF) is:
  1) 15m introductions & goals
  2) 45m prompt inventory deep-dive (we'll annotate guardrails inline)
  3) 30m structured-output alignment (schema + validation)
  4) 30m ops & load-test plan (Ben will run through runbook)
  5) 30m timeboxed live-run and Q&A

- Pre-reqs from Acme:
  • Finalized list of attendees and timezones (we need a calendar invite owner)
  • Mark any prompts that contain PII or regulated data fields (column in the CSV is fine)
  • A single Slack channel or email alias for real-time run coordination during the load test

Ben — can you confirm ops availability for both windows and the rough load-test cadence you'd like? Marissa — I'll hand off calendar + agenda ownership to you when we lock the date.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_kickoff_agenda.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on workshop — ops/load-test details

Priya / Mina — quick ops note from my side.

We can support either window but prefer Thu Apr 22 16:00–19:00 UTC (your Thu 09:00–12:00 PDT) because it gives us a full day to stage. A few specifics so Acme can prepare:

- Recommended load-test window (non-production routing): Sun Apr 25 22:00–02:00 UTC (4-hour window) — short bursts, ramp to target concurrency.
- Target concurrency for initial run: 60 concurrent sessions, sustained for 10 minutes at peak, then step-down.
- Token guidance: plan for peaks of 2–6k tokens per request for a small subset (we'll simulate using sampled prompts).
- We will need: a list of 10 representative prompt IDs from your CSV and a flag for any that must not be persisted.

I'll draft a short runbook and attach (loadtest_runbook.md). During the workshop we'll run a single 10–15 minute live sample with reduced concurrency to validate structured outputs and guardrails.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: loadtest_runbook.md (MD, 18KB)
